P1.evidence: The only genuine setter read-back in the batch, and it landed: "Kim gave me a little bit of a head start anyway. He said you were more so focused on like health and longevity rather than, you know, looking like you're ready to go to the beach in Miami" — prospect: "most importantly, yeah, most importantly, it's that." The frame was two-part rather than four — "I just want to get a good idea where you're at, what it is you do want. If there's alignment and coaching would be a good thing, we can talk about it. If not, that's fine as well" — with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need', and agreement was assumed from "Sure. Sure." rather than asked for. Open question ran clean: "From your perspective, like what were you hoping we could help you with potentially?"

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline of the batch, still with holes. Injuries and limitations were asked directly — "Are there any areas... that you're like, well, this could be improved, this is getting worse?" — surfacing the torn right ankle ligament and the desk-job lower back, though the 'how long' half was never asked. Training week was mapped in detail and used to build a real schedule around match days. Diet was asked properly: "the last thing I would check up on is your diet what kind of stuff are you eating typically." But age, height and weight were never asked — age was volunteered in the prospect's opening monologue. Work was never asked either; "Since I work in private equity, so I have a desk job" was volunteered, and the only ownership question came at 00:28:33, after the price, and was asked for tax-invoicing purposes. No general health-conditions question, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Surface only. The six-month question was asked — "If you were to fast forward six months... what is really the outcome that you are going for?" — and produced mobility and muscle mass, which the rep reflected back accurately ("So it's the mobility and it's the muscular gain"). Then it stopped. The bridge question was never asked, 'what does moving better actually do for you' was never asked, and 'who else does that impact' was never asked — on a call with a 35-year-old who volunteered in his first two minutes that he is married and actively trying for children, and whose own framing was health and longevity. The deepest available lever in the whole batch sat untouched, and the phase where the buying decision is supposed to be made produced nothing to hold against the IPO objection twenty minutes later.

P4.evidence: Well run. "What have you noticed from the times you have done it being like the big reasons why you end up dropping off?" followed by "is there anything else or are they the two things that you notice the most?" The prospect named the gap himself and ranked it: crowded performative gyms, then — "probably that's number one" — never having been followed by a coach, then life events. What is missing is the closing move: the rep solved it for him on the spot ("you don't have to go to the gym with kettlebells... if you get a coach that solves the other problem") rather than letting the cost of the gap sit, and never ran the 'the information isn't the problem' line even though the prospect had handed it over ("I've been always auto-didact online researching").

P5.evidence: Absent. The rep went from root cause into "I feel like I get where you're at" and then the philosophy pitch. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the phase that would have decided the call: the prospect's stated reservation was that a heavy year makes it a bad time to start, and the counter to that is a cost-of-inaction frame that was never built.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before presenting. "How do you feel about it?" after the walk-through is not the belief question, and the all-in question was never asked. The rep did run one good diagnostic after the deferral — "is it a decision of if I should do it, or is it which option to go for?" — which produced the real answer (all three: whether, which, and when). That is the question P6 exists to force before the price, not after it.

P11.evidence: No payment collected and no payment link sent. The onboarding call was negotiated down to a specific slot — Monday 1 June, 7:15pm Switzerland — and then explicitly not booked, correctly per policy: "gotta like onboard you first take payment and stuff like that... so I wouldn't be able to book it in now." Worth noting against the Robert Castillo call four days earlier, where an onboarding slot was booked on an unpaid commitment; the rep applied opposite rules in the same week. No agreement email, nothing signed, no welcome email, Skool link or questionnaire mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: "I'd have to think about it. Most likely it's going to be the 12, but I'd have to think about it." The rep folded on contact — "that's all good, man. That's all good. How long do you feel like you need?" — and immediately changed subject to tax invoicing. None of the core moves ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision'. The one thing he did run, three minutes later, was the decision-type probe ('if I should do it, or which option'), which is the most useful question on the call and should have come first, not last.

The clearest OD trigger in the batch and it got no play at all. "we're planning for an IPO of our group... it's a very heavy process, I'm in the lead of it... I don't want to start and pause it. It doesn't really make sense." The rep's entire response was "That makes sense. That's fine" and "Yeah, no, I appreciate it. All right, cool." Not run: 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled' — which was available and true, since the rep had already explained that programmes can be paused and weeks credited back ("we can pause the program and you just get the week back if needs be"). He had the answer in hand from eight minutes earlier and did not use it.

"is there any flexibility on a monthly payment?" Read in context this is a finance professional structuring a purchase rather than a prospect who cannot pay, and the rep's answer — upfront, or 50/50 within 90 days, or $1,200/month at a $1,200 premium — was commercially clean. But none of the play ran: no isolate, no open-wallet framing, no financial picture. Recorded as a miss for completeness while noting the play was probably not the right tool here; the more useful observation is that a monthly option carrying a 20% surcharge was quoted live.

Script gap. The prospect asked, unprompted, whether kettlebells are recommended for women — "by the way I'll have a follow-up question, is that recommended for women as well, kettlebells? but we can get back to that" — referring to an athletic wife who does pilates and yoga. It was never revisited by either party. There is no scripted move for a partner or referral opening surfaced mid-discovery, and this one was left on the table entirely.

notes: The best-qualified prospect in the batch and the process ran out at exactly the point that mattered. Baseline and root cause were the rep's strongest work; then P3 stopped at 'mobility and muscle', P5 was skipped entirely, and P6 never happened, so when the IPO landed there was no cost of inaction to weigh it against and the rep simply agreed with him. Coach one thing here: the pause-and-credit policy he had already explained was the complete answer to the only real objection on the call, and he did not connect them.
